clue.text: Arrange a nice time without pressure? Job didn't suffer from it

indicators.note: to arrange things is to put them into a new order, so the letters get reordered

parts.note: taken as written
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone wants to fix up a relaxed, pressure-free outing, and a note on the patience of Job follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'lacking' but here means 'outside', so P joins the letters of A NICE TIME before they are rearranged. The definition alludes to the proverbial patience of the biblical Job.
explanation.definitionFit: Job is the Bible's model of endurance, so restless lack of patience is the one failing he never showed.

clue.text: Like material for writer that's popular — okay, but oddly lacking

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: dropping the letters in odd positions keeps only the second, fourth and so on

parts.note: the even letters of the word, its odd ones removed

explanation.surface: Someone approves of a popular writing material, with a grudging 'okay, but'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink is the writer's material, and inky means resembling or stained with it.

clue.text: Expert appearing on channel, as result

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
a duct is a channel or tube

explanation.surface: An expert turns up on a TV channel to report a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests television, but it is a pipe or conduit.
explanation.definitionFit: A product is the outcome or consequence of a process, as in 'the product of hard work'.

clue.text: Safe place during crossing, if craft at sea is secure

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, part of the jumbled letters
taken as written, the rest of the jumbled letters
to land a deal or fish is to secure it

explanation.surface: A sailor hopes for a safe haven in the crossing, if the boat at sea is made secure.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a sea crossing, but the crossing is a road crossing; the anagram indicator sits in the middle of its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic island is a raised refuge in the road where pedestrians can wait safely midway across.

clue.text: Some churchmen listening join service

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are taken, a run inside the words

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Clergymen who are listening decide to join a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The church setting makes 'service' sound like worship; it is military service.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up for the armed forces, joining military service.

clue.text: Players joining club that's resistant to change

parts.note: the cast is the set of players in a show
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: Players sign up with a sports club known for refusing to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a team the players join; it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast-iron, figuratively, means firm and unbreakable, as in a cast-iron guarantee that will not be altered.

clue.text: Prophecies delivered in a couple of seconds

parts.note: taken as written
MO is a moment, an informal second, and S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Predictions are handed down in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The two seconds are two different words for one: MO, as in 'half a mo', and the unit symbol S.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a book of the Old Testament recording the prophecies of the prophet of that name.

clue.text: Gruesome result of vehicle going into female runner

indicators.note: something that goes into another thing ends up inside it

parts.note: a mare is a female horse, a racing runner
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A grisly outcome when a car ploughs into a woman out jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: The runner is a horse in a race, not a jogger.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means dwelling on death in a grim, horrifying way, a close synonym for gruesome.

clue.text: Cut of beef produced by piratical cook on edge

parts.note: Long John Silver is the pirate who serves as ship's cook in Treasure Island
a side is an edge or margin

explanation.surface: A joint of beef is served up by a pirate chef standing on the brink.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverside is a British butcher's cut from the outer part of the hindquarter, often salted or roasted.

clue.text: Roadblock ultimately not any obstacle for smart alec

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
no means not any, as in 'no money'
a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: A roadblock turns out to be no real barrier to a clever person.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is someone who behaves as if they know everything, just like a smart alec.

clue.text: Social changes engulfing team-leader that's resigned

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so one piece goes inside the other
the word changes, so its letters are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the first letter of team

explanation.surface: Social reforms swallow the team captain, who quits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resigned' suggests stepping down from the job, but it means accepting one's lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stoical means enduring hardship without complaint, the calm acceptance of someone resigned to fate.

clue.text: Scientific type with a lot of fliers in his study

definitions.text: Scientific type with a lot of fliers in his study

parts.words: Scientific type with a lot of fliers in his study
parts.note: surface reading: a researcher whose office is strewn with leaflets or flyers
setter's reading: the fliers are birds, the subject he studies

explanation.walkthrough: Fliers sounds like handbills piled in a study room; here the study is a field of science and the fliers are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: This scientist specialises in birds, the creatures that fly, so many fliers make up his field of research.

clue.text: Not hot, not cool

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hot as in currently trendy, negated
second meaning: cool as in stylish, negated

explanation.walkthrough: Hot and cool look like opposites, so 'not hot, not cool' sounds like lukewarm; in slang both mean in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot and cool are both slang for trendy, so anything neither is out of style, out of fashion.

clue.text: Resident in hospital, to some extent exemplary worker

parts.note: taken as written
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
a bit means somewhat, to some extent
the ant is the proverbial model of industry

explanation.surface: A hospital patient is, up to a point, a model employee.
explanation.walkthrough: The ant is held up as a model of hard work in Proverbs ('Go to the ant, thou sluggard').
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant is someone who lives in a place, a resident of it.

clue.text: Observe water or steam?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to spot or see

definitions.note: cryptic: these are water in forms that are not ice
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: liquid or vapour is water that is not frozen

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: split the answer as NOT ICE, which describes water in its other two states.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice is to observe or perceive; and water or steam is H2O in any state but the frozen one.

clue.text: In favour of lock to make building hard to break into

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: Someone backs fitting a lock so a building can resist burglars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' pairs naturally with 'break into' as security hardware, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress is a heavily fortified stronghold designed to withstand attack and entry.

clue.text: Abuse is included in matter that needs to be sorted

indicators.note: something needing sorting is in disorder and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mistreatment is part of an issue that must be dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: IS goes among the letters of MATTER, and the whole lot is then shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse someone is to treat them badly, which is what mistreat means as a verb.

clue.text: Puzzle having this kind of clue, mostly something idiosyncratic

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the clue itself sits in the across list
a tic is a quirk or habitual twitch

explanation.surface: A puzzle featuring clues like this one, largely a quirky thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This kind of clue' is self-referential: the clue is an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a word puzzle in which initial letters of lines spell out a word or message.

clue.text: Hold back or take action following let?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to keep in store for later
second meaning: in tennis a let means the point is replayed, so the player must serve again

explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' looks like 'permit'; it is the tennis call when a serve clips the net and must be taken again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve is to keep something back; split as RE-SERVE, it is serving once more after a let in tennis.

clue.text: Playwright creating conflict between company and director, initially

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
war is armed conflict

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dramatist stirs up a feud between his theatre company and its director.
explanation.walkthrough: Noël Coward was an English playwright, author of Private Lives and Blithe Spirit. The clue's 'between' only places the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël Coward was a celebrated twentieth-century English dramatist and wit.

clue.text: Decide not to vote, collecting a black mark

indicators.note: to collect something is to take it in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: taken as written
a stain is a mark or blemish
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone refrains from voting and earns a black mark for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'a black mark' is split: A and the word for mark hold B between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to deliberately refrain, especially to decline to cast a vote.

clue.text: Capital in bank a racketeer deposited

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow
deposited means lodged within, reinforcing that the letters sit inside

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: Money a gangster stashed in the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like the money being banked; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the capital city of Turkey.

clue.text: Sudden noise when corrupt hosts repeatedly beat us

indicators.note: to host is to take in a guest, so one piece holds another
something corrupt is spoilt or distorted, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then scrambled
to tan is to beat or thrash, and it appears twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sudden racket as crooked hosts keep thrashing us.
explanation.walkthrough: To tan someone's hide is to give them a beating, which is why 'beat' supplies a short word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Instantaneous means happening in an instant, without any delay, so sudden.

clue.text: Want work to make dough, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word's sound, not its spelling

parts.note: kneading is working dough with the hands

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a job that pays good money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dough' looks like slang for money; it is bread dough.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to want or lack it.

clue.text: A contest for couples holding hands cut short

parts.note: taken as written
bridge is a card game played in partnerships, each player holding a hand of cards

explanation.surface: A couples' contest of hand-holding is brought to an early end.
explanation.walkthrough: Hand-holding couples suggests romance; the hands are hands of cards, the couples bridge partners.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, cutting it down.

clue.text: Get excited, setting it in ornamental stone

indicators.note: a jeweller sets a gem inside a mount, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: agate is a banded semi-precious stone
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets worked up while mounting a piece in a decorative gem.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to become stirred up or campaign excitedly; the intransitive sense means get worked up.

clue.text: The fourth of July, for people in general

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: fourth of points to a single letter at that position in the next word

parts.note: the fourth letter of the month name

explanation.surface: Independence Day is a holiday for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fourth of July' looks like the American holiday; it is THE plus the fourth letter of July.
explanation.definitionFit: They is used impersonally for people at large, as in 'they say it will rain'.

clue.text: No longer bent, reportedly, so economically challenged

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: something no longer bent has been made straight

explanation.surface: A crook has gone straight, it is said, and is now hard up as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' also suggests dishonest, giving the surface its reformed crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Straitened circumstances are those of poverty or hardship, short of money.
